dialogues.speaker: Granny Chu
dialogues.text: Heh... Neither could I, in the beginning.

dialogues.speaker: Granny Chu
dialogues.text: But somehow, now that decades have gone by, and even though my hearing has steadily gotten worse over the years... finally, I have started to be able to hear him...

dialogues.speaker: Granny Chu
dialogues.text: It's so wonderful that the legend is true. It means I have not been waiting here in vain all these years.

response.speaker: Granny Chu
response.text: My husband. A muscular man with bronze-colored skin...

response.speaker: Granny Chu
response.text: He was like a child when he proposed to me, though. He took it all so seriously, insisting that he wanted to grow old together with me. Heh.

response.speaker: Granny Chu
response.text: We grew up in the same village. It was a fishing village, and we made our living off the sea.

response.speaker: Granny Chu
response.text: We'd been married for four years when one day, we hit a terrible sea storm. He tied me to the battered boat to make sure I would stay afloat...

response.speaker: Granny Chu
response.text: I drifted all night and ended up here, where I crawled to safety. But my chance to honor our promise to grow old together was gone...

response.speaker: Granny Chu
response.text: If you close your eyes and listen carefully to a conch shell, you will hear the sound of the sea... You know about that, right?

response.speaker: Granny Chu
response.text: Well. I thought to myself, my husband never returned from the sea in the end... I wondered if he said any parting words for me...

response.speaker: Granny Chu
response.text: So I moved into this conch lodge, and have been waiting ever since...

response.speaker: Granny Chu
response.text: Waiting for the day I hear his voice between the crashing of the waves...
